recipes.name: Aussie Chicken
ingredients_raw: 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves - pounded to 1/2 inch thickness

steps.text: Rub chicken breasts with seasoning salt; cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Cook bacon in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until crisp. Drain on paper towels; set aside.
Combine mustard, honey, corn syrup, mayonnaise, and dried onion flakes in a medium bowl; refrigerate 1/2 and set remaining 1/2 aside.

Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add chicken; cook until browned, 3 to 5 minutes per side. Transfer breasts to a 9x13-inch baking dish. Top each breast with remaining 1/2 honey-mustard sauce; layer mushrooms and bacon on top. Sprinkle with shredded cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until cheese is melted and chicken juices run clear, about 15 minutes. Garnish with parsley; serve with reserved 1/2 honey-mustard sauce.

raw_recipe.headline: Aussie Chicken
raw_recipe.description: This Aussie chicken recipe features chicken breasts topped with mushrooms, bacon, and cheese cooked in a honey, mustard, mayonnaise, and onion sauce.

video.description: In this video, we prepare a version of the famous, steakhouse chicken. The chicken is first seared on the stove-top, then topped with a sweet honey mustard sauce, cheese, mushrooms and bacon and baked in the oven.

review.reviewBody: I've been visiting this website for a long time, but this is my first review. Just had to tell you,found this in the "Daily Recipes" section, took it home and made if for dinner last night. My husband, a former chef, mumbled thru his second bite, "Keeper". High praise indeed! I took advice from earlier reviewers, marinated the chicken in worchester sauce, lime juice and garlic (NOT and optional ingredient in our house), left out the light corn syrup (never use it) and used a good stone ground mustand. Found the "zing" some of the others were looking for. I think the corn syrup is just too much sweet with the honey to stand up to the mustard. Served it over thin spinich noodles, there was no leftover sauce. This is on the menu the next time we entertain. Thanks!!!

As someone who has worked for this particular restaurant for 10 years, I'm telling you if you want it authentic, grill the chicken first with just a salt and pepper blend seasoning, then layer the honey mustard sautéed seasoned mushrooms, bacon whole then Monterey Jack and CHEDDAR cheese.... at least that's how they make it there :)

I used chicken tenderloins, omitted the corn syrup, sauteed the mushrooms in the bacon grease and after removing them, browned the seasoned chicken in the same pan, then put them in a 8 x 8 baking dish. After spreading the sauce on the browned chicken, I covered them with the sauteed mushrooms and instead of leaving the bacon in strips, I crumbled it and sprinkled on top of the mushrooms. I used shredded pepper jack cheese, covered the pan with foil and baked for 15 minutes. I then removed the foil and continued to back the chicken for 15 additional minutes uncovered. This was awesome!

Loved this recipe! I did marinate the chicken in equal parts Worcestershire sauce and Kraft zesty Italian. I was planning on cooking it that night and ended up not being able to cook it till the next evening so it marinated for 24 hours. I did not use any corn syrup. I limit my carbs so used Pyure sugar free harmless honey, and then after reading the reviews I decided to use honey mustard and stone ground mustard combo. I put it over cauliflower rice that I sautéed with onion powder and garlic salt. It was absolutely delicious and keto friendly and my husband loved it as well.?

I've made this recipe several times and have adjusted it to my liking. I sautee the mushrooms in the leftover bacon fat with a touch of butter, I use less seasoned salt, I skip the corn syrup and only use half the sauce eliminating the reserved portion. Finally, I use much, much less cheese, and cover it for baking. We love this dish!

No time to marinate. Didn’t use corn syrup as the two lost helpful reviews suggested. Used one pan for everything. Added minced garlic to sauce. Subbed graded cheddar and mozzarella and added the 2nd half of the cheese about 5mins from serving. Took some time but difficult and the result was well worth it

After reading other reviews, I eliminated the corn syrup entirely and cut the honey down to 2 Tbs. It was still sweet enough for us. I will admit that I usually cut down on sweetener with most recipes. I also cooked the bacon in a large skillet, drained some of the bacon grease and fried the chicken in the grease left in the skillet. This will be joining my list of favorites.

Made the recipe more less as written. Used onion powder instead of onion flakes and extra honey instead of corn syrup. I did as many reviewers suggested and cooked the bacon in a frypan, took out all but 2 tablespoons bacon fat and cooked the mushrooms, I added the extra seasonings one reviewer suggested including onion powder, garlic powder, pepper, and paprika, removed the mushrooms, added the extra oil back in, and fried the chicken. I cooked it for five minutes on each side in the pan and 15 minutes in the oven and it came out completely cooked. I Can’t imagine cooking it for any more time as some reviewers suggested. The key must be pounding the chicken breast to 1/2 inch thick. Next time I might cover the pan with foil before baking and remove it for just the last minute or two.

Absolutely delicious! I modified a bit for two people - only used two chicken breasts and didn't halve, but did pound until 1/2 in. thickness. We bought marinated breasts from Wegmans that were brown sugar flavored, which paired well with the rest of the ingredients. I used half the amount of the rest of the ingredients, and didn't add corn syrup as I felt the honey would bring enough sweetness. It was perfect. Next time I'll chop the mushrooms into smaller pieces before spreading on top. Will be making again!

Made this last night. I cut everything in half for the sauce except for the onion flakes. Also sautéed the mushrooms in fat from bacon and seared chicken in same skillet. 1 pan for everything. 20 mins in the oven. Also used Dijon, will add more next time. Was still a bit sweet tasting. But overall tasted great.
Absolutely great! One dish meal! Husband pronounced it "Absolutely fabulous." I made everything in my cast iron skillet then placed in oven to finish.
I’ve been making this recipe for years now. It is one of our favorites. We like to use the seeded ground mustard instead of yellow. This is so tasty!
I have made this a few times; however, you should use dijon mustard. That is what Outback Steakhouse uses. Also, I did not use corn syrup. There is no need for it, in my opinion.

Followed the recipe as posted. It was delicious, everyone loved it and will make again. Notes for next time though - had more than enough sauce for the amount of chicken, 4 average sized breaststroke, about 800g. -also more than enough cheese Next time I'd either cut the sauce and cheese in 1/2 or use 1/2 as much more or double the chicken.

My husband and boys thought it was ok. Hubs thought he would prefer brown mustard since he doesn't care for anything too sweet. I wish I would have read some of the reviews ahead of time and I probably would have left out the corn syrup! Anyhow, they all ate it without complaining. I left off the mushrooms, since they would have just gotten picked off anyway (except for me). I also halved the amount of honey mustard sauce since I know my family and knew they wouldn't want any extra.

We all liked this a lot. After the first time making it, I omitted the onion flakes (didn't like the texture) and the corn syrup (sweet enough without the syrup) in the honey mustard. I pound my chicken breasts thin so you get a better ratio of "the good stuff" (bacon, mushrooms and cheese!)
My family doesn't like mushrooms so I omitted that. I also added pepper and garlic powder to my chicken. We have been making this for a while now, we love this dish.
Easy to make! Gets a lot of frustration out banging on the chicken. Lol
